subject: Chemistry
source_note: TIE (2023), Chemistry Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education Form I-IV

topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry

sub_topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
competences: (a) Describe the mole concept (comparison of the mole with other units of measurements and molar quantities of substances)
(b) Explain Avogadro’s law in relation to molar quantities
(c) Explain the principles of volumetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions and volumetric calculations)
(d) Describe the applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings as in soft drinks and cocktail making, medicine and in agriculture
(e) Explore the basic tenets of ionic theory and electrolysis (ionic theory, mechanism of electrolysis and laws of electrolysis)
(f) Describe the preparation and properties of various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides and sulphates of metals)
(g) Describe the oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia, and carbon dioxide)

objectives.text: (a) Describe the mole concept (comparison of the mole with other units of measurements and molar quantities of substances)
objectives.resources: Analytical balance, different chemicals, and videos, animations, simulations, pictures/ wall, charts illustrating the molar mass of elements
objectives.assessment_criteria: The mole concept is clearly decribed

objectives.text: (b) Explain Avogadro’s law in relation to molar quantities
objectives.assessment_criteria: The Avogadro’s Law is clearly explained and correctly applied in calculating molar quantities

objectives.text: (c) Explain the principles of volumetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions and volumetric calculations)
objectives.resources: Analytical balance, pipette, burette, volumetric flasks, beakers, distilled water, petri dish, watch glass, funnels, wash bottles, HCl, H SO , 2 4 HNO , 3 CH COOH, 3 NaOH, Ca(OH) , 2 Na CO , 2 3 NaHCO 3
objectives.assessment_criteria: The principles of volumetric analysis are clearly explained

objectives.text: (d) Describe the applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings as in soft drinks and cocktail making, medicine and in agriculture
objectives.resources: Pipettes, burettes, volumetric flasks, beakers, distilled water, petri dish, watch glass, funnels, wash bottles, backing powder, vinegar, processed juice, antacids tablets and suspensions, fertiliser, NaOH, HCl, H SO , HNO , 2 4 3 CH COOH, 3 Ca(OH) , 2 Na CO and 2 3 NaHCO 3
objectives.assessment_criteria: The applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings are clearly described

objectives.text: (e) Explore the basic tenets of ionic theory and electrolysis (ionic theory, mechanism of electrolysis and laws of electrolysis)
objectives.resources: Electrolytic cells, pencils, battery (dry cells), connecting wire, distilled water, acid, H SO , 2 4 CuSO , 4 ZnSO , NaCl, 4 KCl, and simulations or videos, diagrams, pictures, wall charts, illustrating principles of ionic theory and electrolysis
objectives.assessment_criteria: The basic principles of ionic theory and electrolysis are clearly described

objectives.text: (f) Describe the preparation and properties of various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides and sulphates of metals)
objectives.resources: Periodic table, lead metal, iron strips, magnesium nitrate, zinc sulphate, lead nitrate, copper sulphate, silver nitrate, magnesium ribbon, aluminium foil, laboratory glassware, water trough, flasks, gas jars, kipps apparatus, combustion tube, heat sources, hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid and the first 20 elements of the periodic table
objectives.assessment_criteria: The preparation and properties of various compounds of metals are clearly described

objectives.text: (g) Describe the oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia, and carbon dioxide)
objectives.resources: Wall charts and pictures showing some important oxidation reactions, periodic table, oxygen gas, hydrogen gas, chlorine gas, hydrogen chloride gas, sulphur dioxide gas, nitrogen gas, ammonia gas, carbon dioxide gas, coloured flower, dyes, hydrogen sulphide, Iron(II) chloride, potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate
objectives.assessment_criteria: Oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds are clearly described

sub_topics.title: Conduct experiments in Chemistry
competences: (b) Perform experiments on the applications of electrolysis in corrosion inhibition and purification of metals
(c) Use appropriate software to sketch the set-ups of experiments
(d) Prepare various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides, and sulphates)
(e) Demonstrate oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metallic compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia and carbon dioxide)
(f) Prepare sulphuric acid from sulphur dioxide

objectives.resources: Analytical balance, pipette, burette, volumetric flasks, beakers, distilled water, laboratory glassware, funnels, wash bottles, NaOH, HCl, H SO , 2 4 HNO , 3 CH COOH, 3 Ca(OH) , 2 Na CO and 2 3 NaHCO 3
objectives.assessment_criteria: Experiments on volumetric analysis are performed correctly

objectives.text: (b) Perform experiments on the applications of electrolysis in corrosion inhibition and purification of metals
objectives.resources: Graph papers, sand papers, dry cells Li-ion (3 V &6 V), Lead acid cells (12 V, 5 Ah-7 Ah), Sulphuric acid, copper(II) sulphate, copper ores and sheets, spoon, copper wires, sodium chloride, graphite rods plate, aluminium ores, gold, zinc, impure copper plates, chloride/ sulphate, iron plates, distilled water, potassium dichromate, coulometer, pure copper rods, ammeter, voltmeter, and 100 mL and 250 mL beakers
objectives.assessment_criteria: Experiments on the applications of electrolysis in corrosion, inhibition and purification of metals are correctly performed

objectives.text: (c) Use appropriate software to sketch the set-ups of experiments
objectives.assessment_criteria: The set-ups of experiments are correctly sketched using Chemistry software

objectives.text: (d) Prepare various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides, and sulphates)
objectives.resources: Periodic table, lead metal, iron strips, magnesium nitrate, zinc sulphate, lead nitrate, copper sulphate, silver nitrate, magnesium ribbon, aluminium foil, water trough, laboratory glassware, flasks, gas jars, Kipps apparatus, combustion tube, heat sources, hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid and the first 20 elements of the periodic table
objectives.assessment_criteria: Various compounds of metals are correctly prepared

objectives.text: (e) Demonstrate oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metallic compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia and carbon dioxide)
objectives.resources: Periodic table, oxygen gas, hydrogen gas, chlorine gas, hydrogen chloride gas, sulphur dioxide gas, nitrogen gas, ammonia gas, carbon dioxide gas, coloured flower, dyes, hydrogen sulphide, iron (II) chloride, potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate and videos, animations or simulations, wall charts and pictures illustrating some important oxidation reactions
objectives.assessment_criteria: Oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds are correctly demonstrated

objectives.text: (f) Prepare sulphuric acid from sulphur dioxide
objectives.resources: Wall charts showing the laboratory / industrial preparation of sulphuric acid, sulphur dioxide, distilled water, delivery tubes and flasks with side arms
objectives.assessment_criteria: Sulphuric acid from sulphur dioxide is correctly prepared

topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of basic principles of extraction of metals

sub_topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of the principles of extraction of metals
competences: (a) Describe the extraction of iron from its ore (ores, stages, and methods of extraction)

objectives.text: (a) Describe the extraction of iron from its ore (ores, stages, and methods of extraction)
objectives.resources: Wall charts showing the metals ores and their methods for extraction, and real ores for metals present in Tanzania
objectives.assessment_criteria: The methods for iron extraction from its ore are clearly described

sub_topics.title: Conduct a project in Chemistry
competences: (a) Design and carry-out a simple research project in Chemistry

objectives.text: (a) Design and carry-out a simple research project in Chemistry
objectives.resources: Library resources and videos, animations or simulations illustrating simple projects in chemistry
objectives.assessment_criteria: A simple research project in Chemistry is designed and developed correctly
